item.title: Blue poles heads west
item.content:
One of the national collection’s most iconic and cherished paintings, Blue poles, will travel across the country thanks to the Albanese Labor Government’s Sharing the National Collection program.

The work, which has never been seen in Western Australia, will go on display at the Art Gallery of Western Australia in Perth from April to September 2027.

Valued in 2023 at $500 million, Blue poles by American Abstract Expressionist artist, Jackson Pollock was purchased by the Australian Government in 1973.

This is the first time the painting has been loaned to an Australian venue by the National Gallery since 2003. With critical capital works already underway at the gallery, the loan will ensure that the work remains on display rather than being placed into storage.

As of 30 June 2026, more than 2.1 million Australians have engaged with more than 327 Sharing the National Collection loans which includes Australian and international works to 42 galleries and cultural venues across every state and territory.

The reaction from audiences and venue partners has been overwhelmingly positive with galleries reporting increases in visitor numbers of up to 51% for their exhibitions showcasing works from the national collection.

This includes sharing more than 50 pieces by legendary American artist Andy Warhol – including his iconic Campbell’s Soup and life-size Elvis works – with the Wanneroo Regional Gallery in 2024, which saw a 750 per cent increase in visitor numbers in the first four months.

Quotes attributable to the Prime Minister, Anthony Albanese

“Blue poles changed our nation, so it makes sense that the nation gets to see it.

“The national collection belongs to every Australian – no matter where they live.

“That’s why we’re sending Blue poles to Perth, making sure the west can enjoy this masterpiece and important part of our national story.”

Quotes attributable to the Minister for the Arts, Tony Burke

“Blue poles was railed against at the time as a waste of money and has proven itself to be one of the smartest investments the National Gallery has ever made.

“The greatest works in the world shouldn’t only be seen in private collections. We are a proud and important creative nation. Australians have a right to know that our national collection is world class, just as they have a right to know that as a national collection, it won't only live in Canberra but will be shared with the whole of the nation.”

Quotes attributable to the National Gallery of Australia, Dr Nick Mitzevich

“When Jackson Pollock’s Blue poles entered the national collection, it signalled ambition, confidence and belief in the importance of art to national life. More than 50 years later, sharing this extraordinary work with audiences across Australia sustains that vision.

“Through the Sharing the National Collection program and with the support of the Australian Government, we are proud to bring one of the Gallery’s most significant works to Australian audiences in Western Australia – who otherwise may never have the opportunity to see it.”

Sharing the National Collection is part of Revive, Australia’s National Cultural Policy.
